overview: My primary research interest is in the intersection between cognitive disorders and medical illness, particularly applied to the aging process. My fascination with cognition and its disorders began with my neuroanatomy class in the first year of medical school, where I first began to understand brain-behavior relationships. This also led to my first research experience, where my mentor, Dr. Jim Hutchins, instilled in the view of the brain as the “great unknown” and a contagious eagerness to solve its mysteries. This continued into my clinical training in medical school and psychiatry residency and fellowship, where I truly began to appreciate the relationship of the brain with complex behavior through such illnesses as dementia and delirium. After completing my fellowship, I began to work with Dr. Paula Trzepacz, a nationally known expert in delirium, who helped solidify my disparate training experiences into a cohesive interest studying the clinical consequences of cognitive disorders that has continued throughout my career.
